entities.name: Methyl ester hydrolysis
observations: The tokenized substrate/product pair shows conversion of an aromatic methyl ester, C(=O)OCH3, to the corresponding carboxylic acid, C(=O)OH, while the nitro group, aryl ether, heteroaromatic rings, and other connectivity are retained.
The transformation is consistent with base-promoted ester saponification followed by acidification.

entities.name: NaOH methanol hydrolysis
observations: A matching reaction record lists sodium hydroxide, methanol, 1,4-dioxane, and citric acid for conversion of the methyl ester to the carboxylic acid.
Methanol and 1,4-dioxane are reaction solvents; citric acid is an acidification/workup reagent. Explicit time, temperature, and isolated yield were not available.

entities.name: Sodium hydroxide
observations: Likely hydrolysis reagent for saponification of the methyl ester in the target reaction.

entities.name: Citric acid
observations: Likely acidification reagent used after saponification to isolate the free carboxylic acid.
